{{short description|Axiom of set theory}}
In mathematics, the '''wholeness axiom''' is a strong axiom of set theory introduced by [[Paul Corazza]] in 2000.<ref>{{citation|title=The Wholeness Axiom and Laver Sequences|first=Paul|last= Corazza|journal=Annals of Pure and Applied Logic |volume=  105|year=2000|issue=1–3|pages= 157–260|doi=10.1016/s0168-0072(99)00052-4|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Statement==
The wholeness axiom states roughly that there is an [[elementary embedding]] ''j'' from the [[Von Neumann universe]] ''V'' to itself. This has to be stated carefully to avoid [[Kunen's inconsistency theorem]] stating (roughly) that no such embedding exists.

More specifically, as Samuel Gomes da Silva states, "the inconsistency is avoided by omitting from the schema all instances of the Replacement Axiom for ''j''-formulas".<ref>Samuel Gomes da Silva, Review of "The wholeness axioms and the class of supercompact cardinals" by Arthur Apter.</ref>
Thus, the wholeness axiom differs from [[Reinhardt cardinal]]s (another way of providing elementary embeddings from ''V'' to itself) by allowing the [[axiom of choice]] and instead modifying the [[axiom of replacement]].
However, {{harvtxt|Holmes|Forster|Libert|2012}} write that Corrazza's theory should be "naturally viewed as a version of [[Zermelo set theory]] rather than [[ZFC]]".<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Holmes | first1 = M. Randall
 | last2 = Forster | first2 = Thomas | author-link2 = Thomas Forster (mathematician)
 | last3 = Libert | first3 = Thierry
 | contribution = Alternative set theories
 | doi = 10.1016/B978-0-444-51621-3.50008-6
 | mr = 3409865
 | pages = 559–632
 | publisher = Elsevier/North-Holland, Amsterdam
 | series = Handb. Hist. Log.
 | title = Sets and extensions in the twentieth century
 | volume = 6
 | year = 2012}}.</ref>

If the wholeness axiom is consistent, then it is also consistent to add to the wholeness axiom the assertion that all sets are [[Ordinal definable set|hereditarily ordinal definable]].<ref name="h"/>
The consistency of stratified versions of the wholeness axiom, introduced by {{harvtxt|Hamkins|2001}},<ref name="h">{{citation

 | doi = 10.1007/s001530050169
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Archive for Mathematical Logic
 | mr = 1816602
 | pages = 1–8
 | title = The wholeness axioms and ''V'' = HOD
 | volume = 40
 | year = 2001| arxiv = math/9902079| s2cid = 15083392 }}.</ref> was studied by {{harvtxt|Apter|2012}}.<ref>{{citation
 | last = Apter | first = Arthur W.
 | doi = 10.4064/ba60-2-1
 | issue = 2
 | journal =  Bulletin of the Polish Academy of Sciences, Mathematics

 | title = The wholeness axioms and the class of supercompact cardinals
 | volume = 60
